output.question: Has Walmart announced layoffs?
output.answer: Yes. The latest specific filing I verified was reported on June 23, 2026: Walmart planned to permanently lay off 306 corporate workers in Sunnyvale, California, effective August 21, 2026. Those cuts were part of a restructuring announced to employees on May 12, 2026, reportedly affecting about 1,000 corporate technology and product roles through layoffs or relocations—not 1,000 confirmed layoffs. Walmart confirmed job eliminations but did not disclose an exact layoff total; that restructuring did not affect retail-store staff.

key_facts.fact: As reported June 23, 2026, Walmart filed notices on June 19 for 306 permanent corporate layoffs across eight Sunnyvale sites, scheduled for August 21, 2026.
The Sunnyvale cuts were part of the broader restructuring announced in May 2026.
Walmart sent employees a restructuring memo on May 12, 2026, and confirmed job eliminations without specifying the exact number of layoffs.
As reported May 13, 2026, approximately 1,000 corporate roles were affected by layoffs or relocations; the figure was not a confirmed layoff count.
The May 2026 restructuring affected corporate positions rather than retail-store staff.

passages.quote: Walmart has filed notices to permanently lay off 306 corporate workers across eight Sunnyvale sites in August, according to California employment records.
Walmart has now confirmed to Fast Company that it is eliminating some roles, without specifying the exact number of positions to be cut.
Walmart is eliminating or relocating about 1,000 corporate positions as it seeks to reduce redundancy in the technology operations across its organization.

caveats: I did not verify a newer layoff announcement after the June 2026 reporting; this does not establish that none occurred.
The approximately 1,000 affected roles included relocations, so that figure should not be described as 1,000 confirmed layoffs.
The August 21 effective date was a planned date in the notices; completion of the layoffs was not independently verified.
The sources opened were reporting on company-provided memos and state filings, rather than the original memo or filing itself.
